source_user: Calculation case 263: a model has 40 layers, 6 KV heads, head dimension 96, sequence length 2560, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 40 × 2560 × 6 × 96 × 2 = 235929600 bytes = 0.219727 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions that must be checked against config.json and the serving engine before this number drives any capacity decision: (1) standard attention with exactly one K tensor and one V tensor per layer, hence the leading factor of 2; (2) num_key_value_heads is the GQA/MQA KV head count, not num_attention_heads; (3) no sliding-window, no cross-attention, and no MLA-style latent compression, any of which invalidates the linear-in-sequence-length model; (4) sequence length means total context (prompt + generated), not prompt alone.

Formula: kv_bytes = 2 (K and V) x num_layers x seq_len x num_kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value.

Substituting: 2 x 40 x 2560 x 6 x 96 x 2 = 235929600 bytes = 225.0000 MiB = 0.219727 GiB (GiB = bytes / 2^30). Dtype assumed: BF16/FP16 (2 bytes/value).

KV is stored in the same 2-byte dtype as activations, so there are no side scale tensors to account for; the payload figure is the whole KV tensor cost.

Boundary conditions the raw figure does not capture, each of which pushes real allocation upward:
- PagedAttention block rounding. With block_size B tokens, allocation is ceil(2560/B) x B tokens, not 2560. At B=16 that is exact here only if 2560 % 16 == 0 (it is); ragged or short requests round up and the waste is bounded by (B-1)/seq_len per sequence.
- Tensor parallelism. KV heads shard across TP ranks only when TP divides num_key_value_heads; with num_kv_heads = 6, TP > 6 either replicates KV per rank or is rejected by the engine, so per-GPU KV does not keep falling as TP grows.
- Prefix caching / radix trees keep blocks alive after a request finishes, so steady-state resident KV exceeds concurrency x per-request KV.
- Speculative decoding and beam search hold KV for draft or candidate branches simultaneously.
- The allocator pre-reserves a KV pool (gpu_memory_utilization in vLLM); the pool, not this per-request number, is what shows up in nvidia-smi.

Capacity use: max concurrency ~= floor(KV_pool_bytes / 235929600), then derate for block rounding and prefix-cache residency. Treat that as an upper bound, not a target.

Falsifiable prediction and how to test it: allocate one request at full context and measure the delta in torch.cuda.memory_allocated() (or the engine's KV block counter). It should equal 235929600 bytes within a few percent. If measured KV is an integer multiple (2x, 4x, ...) of this, the config's KV head count or the factor-of-2 assumption is wrong; if it is far larger and non-integral, block rounding, quantization metadata, or prefix-cache retention is the cause.

Evidence to collect: config.json (num_hidden_layers, num_key_value_heads, head_dim or hidden_size/num_attention_heads), the engine's kv_cache_dtype and block_size, the TP degree, and a measured single-request memory delta. Rollback gate: if measured per-request KV exceeds this estimate by more than 20%, or if the derived max concurrency causes preemption/recompute events in the scheduler log, revert the concurrency setting to the last known-good value before tuning further.
risks: Source gives the arithmetic but never warns that num_kv_heads must come from num_key_value_heads under GQA/MQA; substituting query heads undersizes KV by an integer factor.
No mention of PagedAttention block rounding, so per-request allocation is understated for sequence lengths that are not block-aligned.
TP sharding of KV heads is not discussed; with few KV heads, KV does not shard past num_kv_heads and per-GPU KV stops shrinking.
Prefix caching and speculative decoding retain extra KV, so this per-request figure cannot be multiplied by concurrency to size a pool.
The 'excludes allocator metadata' caveat is vague and gives no measurement or rollback gate.

Serving engine settings: kv_cache_dtype, block_size, gpu_memory_utilization, enable_prefix_caching
Tensor-parallel degree and whether TP divides num_key_value_heads
Measured torch.cuda.memory_allocated() delta (or engine KV block counter) for one full-length request
Scheduler log for preemption/recompute events at the derived concurrency

Assumptions that must be checked against config.json and the serving engine before this number drives any capacity decision: (1) standard attention with exactly one K tensor and one V tensor per layer, hence the leading factor of 2; (2) num_key_value_heads is the GQA/MQA KV head count, not num_attention_heads; (3) no sliding-window, no cross-attention, and no MLA-style latent compression, any of which invalidates the linear-in-sequence-length model; (4) sequence length means total context (prompt + generated), not prompt alone.

Formula: kv_bytes = 2 (K and V) x num_layers x seq_len x num_kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value.

Substituting: 2 x 56 x 2560 x 4 x 128 x 2 = 293601280 bytes = 280.0000 MiB = 0.273438 GiB (GiB = bytes / 2^30). Dtype assumed: BF16/FP16 (2 bytes/value).

KV is stored in the same 2-byte dtype as activations, so there are no side scale tensors to account for; the payload figure is the whole KV tensor cost.

Boundary conditions the raw figure does not capture, each of which pushes real allocation upward:
- PagedAttention block rounding. With block_size B tokens, allocation is ceil(2560/B) x B tokens, not 2560. At B=16 that is exact here only if 2560 % 16 == 0 (it is); ragged or short requests round up and the waste is bounded by (B-1)/seq_len per sequence.
- Tensor parallelism. KV heads shard across TP ranks only when TP divides num_key_value_heads; with num_kv_heads = 4, TP > 4 either replicates KV per rank or is rejected by the engine, so per-GPU KV does not keep falling as TP grows.
- Prefix caching / radix trees keep blocks alive after a request finishes, so steady-state resident KV exceeds concurrency x per-request KV.
- Speculative decoding and beam search hold KV for draft or candidate branches simultaneously.
- The allocator pre-reserves a KV pool (gpu_memory_utilization in vLLM); the pool, not this per-request number, is what shows up in nvidia-smi.

Capacity use: max concurrency ~= floor(KV_pool_bytes / 293601280), then derate for block rounding and prefix-cache residency. Treat that as an upper bound, not a target.

Falsifiable prediction and how to test it: allocate one request at full context and measure the delta in torch.cuda.memory_allocated() (or the engine's KV block counter). It should equal 293601280 bytes within a few percent. If measured KV is an integer multiple (2x, 4x, ...) of this, the config's KV head count or the factor-of-2 assumption is wrong; if it is far larger and non-integral, block rounding, quantization metadata, or prefix-cache retention is the cause.

Evidence to collect: config.json (num_hidden_layers, num_key_value_heads, head_dim or hidden_size/num_attention_heads), the engine's kv_cache_dtype and block_size, the TP degree, and a measured single-request memory delta. Rollback gate: if measured per-request KV exceeds this estimate by more than 20%, or if the derived max concurrency causes preemption/recompute events in the scheduler log, revert the concurrency setting to the last known-good value before tuning further.
risks: Source gives the arithmetic but never warns that num_kv_heads must come from num_key_value_heads under GQA/MQA; substituting query heads undersizes KV by an integer factor.
No mention of PagedAttention block rounding, so per-request allocation is understated for sequence lengths that are not block-aligned.
TP sharding of KV heads is not discussed; with few KV heads, KV does not shard past num_kv_heads and per-GPU KV stops shrinking.
Prefix caching and speculative decoding retain extra KV, so this per-request figure cannot be multiplied by concurrency to size a pool.
The 'excludes allocator metadata' caveat is vague and gives no measurement or rollback gate.
